parts.name: bronchiole
parts.what: A small airway in cross-section: a smooth-muscle ring around the wall, a mucosal lining, and an open lumen with air flowing through. Generic and reusable for any lesson on asthma, COPD or other obstructive airway disease.
events: constrict — the muscle ring tightens, narrowing the lumen
inflame — the mucosal lining swells and thickens
mucus — thick mucus appears in the lumen
relieve — the muscle ring relaxes back and the lumen reopens
parts.accuracy: In an asthma attack the airway smooth muscle tightens (bronchoconstriction), the mucosal lining becomes swollen and inflamed, and the airway produces extra, thicker mucus — together narrowing the lumen and reducing airflow (ledger: GINA 2024 ch.1 'Pathophysiology'; NHS 'Asthma' — Causes). A reliever relaxes the tightened muscle quickly; a preventer reduces the inflammation over time (ledger: NHS 'Asthma' — Treatment; GINA 2024 ch.3 'Reliever medications' / 'Controller medications').

parts.name: inhaler
parts.what: A handheld metered-dose inhaler: canister and mouthpiece. Generic device, reusable wherever a lesson needs to show inhaled medicine being taken (asthma, COPD, any respiratory-drug delivery).
events: puff — the canister is pressed and a fine mist releases from the mouthpiece
parts.accuracy: Reliever inhalers act quickly to relax airway muscle; preventer inhalers are taken regularly (usually daily) to reduce airway inflammation over time, and must be used even when feeling well (ledger: NHS 'Asthma' — Treatment; GINA 2024 ch.3 'Reliever medications' / 'Controller medications' / 'Adherence').
